claims.text: Pre-oxidizing boride-based components to form a continuous Al2O3 layer will improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The untreated initial material has no preformed protective oxide layer.
High-temperature oxidation in air can form a stable, dense alumina scale on the unspecified boride-based component.
Oxidation at approximately 800 °C for about 1 hour in air will produce the intended protective oxide layer.
Typical molten-aluminum plating exposure temperatures are approximately 700–750 °C.
Hundreds of hours of molten-aluminum exposure are representative of service conditions.
Alumina has low diffusivity at elevated temperatures.
Alumina has high chemical stability at elevated temperatures.
A continuous alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier between the boride substrate and molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 scale will slow or prevent molten-aluminum infiltration and reaction with the underlying boride phase.
Preventing direct contact and interdiffusion will reduce dissolution of boride constituents and mitigate corrosion.
Pre-oxidized components will have significantly lower weight loss and surface degradation than untreated boride components during molten-aluminum exposure.
Lower corrosion will increase component stability and longevity.
Untreated boride components suffer higher degradation through direct chemical attack and dissolution in molten aluminum.
Protection will persist up to about 750 °C if the oxide scale remains continuous and intact.
Mechanical damage to the alumina scale may compromise corrosion protection.
Additional fluxing species may compromise corrosion protection.
The protective nature of alumina in high-temperature environments is well established.
A controlled comparison will expose pre-oxidized and untreated specimens to molten aluminum at about 720 °C for 500 hours and compare weight loss, SEM/EDS observations, and XRD results.
Failure of the pre-oxidized specimens to show a statistically significant corrosion-resistance improvement over untreated specimens would falsify the hypothesis.
